title: Interface multi-type paging integration test + parity fixture
description: End-to-end proof that a HasOwner interface implemented by three Northwind ObjectTypes (customer + employee + supplier) can be paginated through loadObjectsOrInterfaces with pageSize=7 without dropping or duplicating any row. The test boots a real Postgres via testcontainers, persists the ontology + interface + object_type_interfaces rows through pkg/oms.PGRepository, seeds per-type Bleve indexes from the Northwind CSV seed, and exercises the preview handler via chi.

seed.pkNamespacing: rows are indexed under '<apiName>:<rawPK>' so employee '1' and supplier '1' never collide in the shared paging map; heap merge then resolves any remaining ties by ObjectType apiName ASC per US-007.

pagination.comment: Per-type buckets are sorted ASC by primary key in the executor; the handler performs an iterative min-heap selection per page using per-type offsets decoded from the inbound MultiTypeCursor. Sub-cursors with offset == len(bucket) are dropped from the emitted token so the wire format shrinks as sub-streams drain.

pageShape.derivation: ceil(129 / 7) = 19 pages; the last page holds 129 - 18*7 = 3 rows.

invariants: no row is visited twice (keyed by ($apiName, $primaryKey))
no row is skipped (sum of perType counts == totalCount)
every non-final page returns exactly pageSize=7 rows
nextPageToken advances strictly on every non-final page
totalCount is stable across all pages
each row exposes $apiName, $primaryKey, $rid, plus every field in select[]

responseShape.nextPageToken: <base64 MultiTypeCursor or omitted on final page>

notes: This fixture documents the wire contract; the integration test is the executable spec. The dedicated parity runner (test/foundry_parity/run.go) will be introduced by the Phase 6 Gate.
Run the integration test with `go test -tags integration ./test/integration/... -run InterfacePaging`. It requires Docker for testcontainers.

The executor still calls the InterfaceResolver injected via *Executor.SetInterfaceResolver; production main.go does not yet wire a PG-backed resolver, so this test ships its own pgInterfaceResolver shim around oms.PGRepository. Follow-up work is tracked under the Phase 6 Gate story to fold that shim into main.

pk namespacing in the fixture (apiName:rawPK) is a test-local choice to keep the 'seen' map unambiguous; it does not change the Foundry wire format assumptions — callers should treat $primaryKey as opaque.
